📖 How to use

  1. Enter your starting balance and annual withdrawal amount.
  2. Set expected investment return and inflation.
  3. Read how many years the money lasts and scan the yearly table.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How does the simulation work?

Each year: balance grows by the investment return, then the withdrawal (raised by inflation) is taken out. The table runs until the balance hits zero or 60 years pass.

How do inflation and returns interact?

Withdrawals rise with inflation each year to preserve purchasing power, while the remaining balance keeps earning the assumed return.

What is the 4% rule?

The classic rule of thumb withdraws 4% of the starting balance in year one (then inflation-adjusted). Use it as the annual withdrawal input to test the rule on your numbers.
